title: Continuous window misstep — quickfire debugging log
content:
Context / symptom:
- After 2026-03-09 canary -> prod rollout for model: rdm-large-v2, we observed a persistent ~25% drop in aggregate tokens/sec for the public inference tier.
- Latency P95 rose from ~180ms -> ~320ms. P99 spiked intermittently to 750–1,200ms.
- No increased error responses (4xx/5xx) seen in API proxy, just throughput degradation and queuing.
- Only noticeable change in rollout: adjusted 'continuous_window_ms' default from 40 -> 15 and enabled 'aggressive_prefill' flag in the deployment spec.

Quick facts (from the dashboard snapshots):
- baseline (pre-change) tokens/sec: ~190k/min
- observed during incident: ~140k/min
- mean inflight requests per worker: pre 2.2 -> post 4.7
- worker utilization: GPU SM util unchanged (~72%), but per-request tail latency higher

First-pass hypothesis (brain dump):
1) Window too small -> more frequent micro-batches -> overhead per-batch increased (kernel launch, KV cache ops).
2) Aggressive prefill interacts poorly with small window: prefill triggers sparse small prefill fills, leading to fragmented KV cache and extra memory copies.
3) Autoscaler reaction: increased apparent latency causes HPA to scale down (scale-to-zero-ish) on some zones and then scale back slowly, creating cycles of underpacking.
4) Router/priority mis-sending short requests to warmed workers and long requests to cold ones thanks to a race in the routing policy.

Commands and traces I ran (notes + obs):
- k get pods -n inference | grep rdm-large-v2 -> saw 6 pods healthy, age 2d
- kubectl logs -n inference runner-pod-82 -c runner | tail -n 200 | grep -E "Batcher|Window|Prefill|evict"
  -> saw repeated: "Batcher: window=15ms triggered create(batch_id=0x8d) size=1" and later "KVCache: eviction_pressure=high count=23"
- strace on runner (short snippet): repeated futex waits around 8–12ms where previously <1ms. Looks like contention on prefill mutex.
- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:8080/metrics | grep tokens_generated -> 2.3e6 over 2m during test (lower than baseline)
- Local load test: wrk -t8 -c250 -d60s --latency "http://ingress/host/generate?model=rdm-large-v2"
  -> baseline container (with window=40ms): mean latency 210ms, requests/sec X
  -> problematic config (window=15ms + aggressive_prefill=true): mean latency 310ms, req/sec -23%

Error/warning snippets captured:
- [runner] WARN 2026-03-09T14:12:05Z Batcher: creating micro-batch that is suboptimal (size=1)
- [kvcache] WARN 2026-03-09T14:12:06Z Evicting 12 entries to free 6MB; high churn
- [allocator] ERROR 2026-03-09T14:12:07Z slow_malloc: took 4.2ms > threshold 1ms
- [router] DEBUG 2026-03-09T14:12:07Z routing decision: prefer_low_latency, fallback=zone-b, selected=zone-a (age_diff=110ms)

Experiments attempted (what I toggled and result):
- Revert continuous_window_ms=15 -> 40 on one canary node: tokens/sec returned to ~96% of baseline on that node, P95 dropped ~90ms. Good sign.
- Disable aggressive_prefill on canary -> no improvement alone. So prefill flag by itself isn't main cause.
- Increase max_batch_delay_ms from 5 -> 20 (keeps window but allows slightly larger grouping): partial improvement, throughput +8% but still below baseline.
- Force Batcher to prefer time-based packing vs count-based: inconsistent results across model variants.
- Temporarily set autoscaler minReplicas to current observed to avoid scale-down: removed scale oscillation but throughput still 10% down. Suggests both packing and scaling interplay.

Notes about telemetry we should add to dashboards (gaps I saw):
- per-pod histogram of actual batch sizes over time (not just avg) -> need to see micro-batch frequency spikes
- lock contention metrics around prefill/kvcache mutexes
- kernel launch overhead per batch (ms) by batch size
- per-request assignment age (time between arrival -> assigned to runner) to detect routing races

Deeper logs / trace snippets I saved (copy below for context):
--- BEGIN LOG SNIPPET ---
[runner] INFO 2026-03-09T14:12:04Z Received request id=urn:rq:0x7a
[runner] DEBUG 2026-03-09T14:12:04Z Batcher: queue_len=3 window_ms=15 last_flush=12ms
[runner] DEBUG 2026-03-09T14:12:04Z Batcher: create batch size=1 id=0x7a (reason=window_expiry)
[kvcache] DEBUG 2026-03-09T14:12:05Z Prefill start id=0x7a tokens=48
[kvcache] WARN 2026-03-09T14:12:05Z Prefill incomplete due to prefill-threshold (got 8/48)
[runner] DEBUG 2026-03-09T14:12:05Z KernelLaunch begin for batch=0x7a size=1
[allocator] ERROR 2026-03-09T14:12:05Z slow_malloc alloc_size=65536 took=4.2ms
--- END LOG SNIPPET ---

Interpretation (quick):
- The window expiry rule is firing often and creating single-request batches. That increases per-batch overhead (kernel launch + allocator pressure). Prefill tries to fetch KV for longer sequences but is clipped by prefill-threshold -> wasted work.
- Allocator slowness suggests memory allocation churn due to many small batches. Could be mitigated by pooling or preallocating scratch space for micro-batches.
- Autoscaler indiscriminately scales by CPU/GPU utilization which doesn't reflect packing inefficiency -> leads to underprovisioned but high-util pods. Need a packing-aware scaling signal (batching efficiency metric).

Short-term mitigations tried / candidates: (actionable, quick)
- Revert continuous_window_ms to 40ms globally (rolled back on 2026-03-10 03:22 UTC) -> restored throughput mostly.
- Add a safety guard in deployment config: min_batch_size=2 for N minutes after rollout to avoid singletons.
- Add host-level preallocated scratch buffer to avoid slow_malloc spikes (requires binary change).
- Adjust HPA to consider 'effective_tokens_per_second' metric (from router) instead of raw GPU util.

Longer-term ideas / follow-ups:
- Fuzz test: simulate many tiny requests to measure allocator behavior and prefill cost per token.
- Add end-to-end integration test for new batching defaults before rollout (CI job that runs a short load test).
- Evaluate switching default window semantics to 'adaptive' (expand when pack rate low, shrink when packing high).
- Telemetry: add batch-size distribution heatmap, kernel-overhead by size, mutex wait time series.

Open questions / TODOs for next pairing session with Liam:
- Can router be made batch-size-aware when choosing target runner? (avoid sending long requests to underpacked nodes)
- Is there existing allocator pooling we can enable quickly? Where is the config? (search codebase for 'prealloc' / 'scratch-pool')
- Check if any infra patch (kernel driver / NVIDIA updates) coincidentally shipped 2026-03-08 -> cross-check with release-engineering.

Random notes-to-self:
- Keep a snapshot of the exact pod env for the canary that behaved well (kubectl describe pod -> save.yaml).
- When reverting configs, wait 10–12 minutes for pack metrics to stabilize before measuring.
- Document rollback decision and timeline in INF-3421 and add links to this note.

Bottom line (TL;DR):
- Root cause appears to be an interaction: unusually small continuous window + prefill behavior -> high micro-batch frequency -> allocator contention and wasted prefill work. Autoscaler amplifies effect by reacting to util instead of packing efficiency. Revert of window rolled back most of the regression. Need telemetry and a packing-aware autoscaling signal to prevent recurrence.

Last edited: 2026-03-11 by Maya R.
